subject: Clarify: 72-hour trigger & telemetry export scope for DPA incident clause
messages:
From: Lina Park <lina.park@finquant.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: security@finquant.com
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA — 72hr notification + telemetry export request

Grace —

Thanks for the quick onboarding call this week. A couple of items FinQuant needs clarified in the DPA before legal will sign:

1) Notification trigger: we require notification within 72 hours of 'actual unauthorized access' or strong evidence of exfiltration.
2) Telemetry export: we need the ability to receive a copy of forensic telemetry (logs, request traces, relevant KV-cache snapshots) into our secured S3 for independent triage. We expect transfer within 72 hours of notification.
3) Subprocessors: please list any third parties that will touch logs (e.g., log aggregators, analytics providers) — we need contact points and SOC2 evidence.

We know this is operationally sensitive, so happy to sign an evidence-protection addendum or an NDA for the forensic package. Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept a limited-scope export that excludes customer content but includes request metadata and header traces?

Lina
Lina Park
Head of Security — FinQuant
lina.park@finquant.com
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Lina Park <lina.park@finquant.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA — 72hr notification + telemetry export request

Lina —

Appreciate the clear asks. Short answers up front: we can meet the 72-hour notification window for confirmed incidents; telemetry export within 72 hours is trickier operationally but may be possible for a narrowly scoped package.

I’ve looped Ben (account lead) and Stephanie (legal/security) to scope contractual language and operational impact. Karthik from infra will need to advise on what "forensic telemetry" practically includes and the safe export mechanism. I attached our current forensic-log-specs.csv that lists the fields we typically collect.

Open questions I want us to resolve before a redline:
- Trigger definition: 'actual unauthorized access' vs 'reasonable belief' — which party owns the initial determination?
- Scope: a limited package (timestamps, request IDs, headers, task traces, anonymized user IDs) vs full request payloads.
- Subprocessors: we will provide a list but will need to redact vendor internal emails.
- Cross-border: if logs contain EU-origin traffic, we need to confirm transfer controls.

Next steps:
- Stephanie, please propose clean contract language that balances FinQuant's need for timely access with Redwood's operational/security constraints.
- Karthik, confirm the earliest timeline we can stage a presigned S3 upload for a subset export.
- Ben, can you schedule a 30-min call with FinQuant this week to walk through the proposed scope?

Thanks — I’ll follow up after we get legal & infra input.

— Grace

Subject: Re: DPA — 72hr notification + telemetry export request

Team —

Context from FinQuant: they operate in regulated finance vertical, high sensitivity to timely evidence. They will probably push for both 72-hour notice and full export within the same window as part of their internal SLAs. Their legal is unlikely to accept 'reasonable belief' as the sole trigger.

Suggested compromise to present on the call:
- Keep 'reasonable belief' as the contractual standard, but add a parallel fast-track for 'notification and limited telemetry transfer within 72 hours upon FinQuant's formal request and mutual escalation if Redwood confirms scope is safe'.
- Define 'limited telemetry' explicitly: request IDs, timestamps, routing headers, anonymized session identifiers, and error traces. No full request bodies unless court order or explicit mutual agreement.
- Operational flow: FinQuant opens an evidence request ticket, Redwood triages and produces a redacted package, we provide a presigned S3 URL (48-72h) with AES-256 encrypted archive.

I drafted a sample clause we can share (attached redlines_v3.docx).

If we position it as a two-tier approach (fast limited export vs full export under legal compulsion), that may protect our ops while giving customer confidence. Happy to join the call.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 13:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA — 72hr notification + telemetry export request

Folks —

Attached are legal redlines and our recommended operational guardrails. Key positions:

1) Trigger language: preserve 'reasonable belief' for Redwood notification obligations. Counterproposal for FinQuant: add a separate voluntary cooperation clause that permits a customer-requested limited export within 72 hours after the customer provides a written request and executes an evidence-handling addendum. This keeps our legal standard while offering a clear operational path.

2) Scope definition (we propose to contractually define 'limited telemetry' as):
   - Immutable metadata: request timestamps, request IDs/trace IDs, status codes, routing headers.
   - Aggregated counters and error traces.
   - Session identifiers pseudonymized using one-way hashing with a salt retained by Redwood (we will not provide the salt).
   - Exclude request/response bodies, embeddings, and derived customer content.

3) Subprocessor handling: require Redwood to provide an up-to-date subprocessor roster and SOC 2 report on request. For any subprocessor that would directly access exported telemetry, we will either: (a) perform an audit, or (b) provide a contact and the subprocessor's attestation.

4) Transfer mechanics & custody: telecoms-presigned S3 (template attached) or secure SFTP to a customer-owned endpoint; all transfers must be encrypted in transit and at rest and logged. Chain-of-custody records will be maintained.

5) Cross-border & data minimization: where EU-origin data exists, apply pseudonymization and export via our EU data center or use approved SCCs.

I attached redlines_v3.docx with explicit clause language and our proposed evidence-handling addendum. Operational notes included in forensic-log-specs.csv.

If FinQuant insists on 'actual unauthorized access' as the only trigger, we risk exposure because a customer may have earlier indicators that meet 'reasonable belief'. The voluntary cooperation path should resolve business need without broadening our legal obligations.

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
From: Lina Park <lina.park@finquant.com>

Subject: Re: DPA — 72hr notification + telemetry export request

Grace / Stephanie / Ben —

Thank you for the thoughtful proposals and the redlines. FinQuant is generally comfortable with the two-tier approach you described, provided the limited telemetry within 72 hours includes:

- Trace IDs and timestamps tied to affected sessions
- HTTP headers and routing metadata (no bodies)
- Error traces and stack snippets related to the event

We also agree to sign an evidence-handling addendum and an NDA for the forensic package. Our priority is being able to start triage quickly — we accept pseudonymized session IDs and presigned S3 as long as the ingestion mechanism is documented and reproducible.

Action items:
- Redwood to share the final redline (incorporating Stephanie's wording) and the presigned S3 template by EOD Monday.
- Schedule a 30-min technical walk-through next Tuesday (prefer 10:00 AM PT) to validate fields in forensic-log-specs.csv.
- Redwood to provide a current subprocessor roster and SOC2 attestation for any vendor that may touch logs.

If you can get the redline and template over, I'll circulate internally and confirm the call.

— Lina
Lina Park
Head of Security — FinQuant
